batch_strategy: Broad-width failure repair combined with same-molecule PE/EA response curves, loading contrasts, and moderate-width local controls.

choices.reason: High predicted V1/V2 widths and late predicted completion make this a useful difficult-region label for a polar acid-like structure at high loading-solvent volume.
The model predicts a broad late interval for this hydrogen-bonding oxime-like molecule; measuring it probes an underconstrained polar chemotype.
A narrow-width m32 point at 1/1 DCM provides a local control for the second m32 point in this batch and helps estimate condition-response slope.
This m79 point extends the molecule's condition response toward 5/1 DCM, complementing measured m79 behavior at a stronger PE-rich ratio.
A low-width halogenated aromatic control at 1/1 DCM supplies a well-behaved local label for separating ordinary interpolation from high-tail failures.
This 2/1 DCM m25 point samples a moderately broad interval in a ketone-rich ester chemotype and complements measured m25 conditions.
The m163 point adds a 2/1 PE condition with nontrivial predicted width, extending measured m163 condition coverage and testing solvent response.
High predicted widths at 5/1 DCM target a polyaromatic structure where model uncertainty may reflect packing and loading effects beyond simple polarity descriptors.
A relatively narrow m52 point at 1/1 PE provides a low-complexity aliphatic bromide control in the PE-rich subset.
This m81 point has broader predicted V1/V2 ranges and complements the second m81 point, allowing a local response estimate across ratio and loading.
The 10/1 PE m14 condition extends a measured m14 ratio series toward stronger elution and tests whether the predictor captures its shift in onset and completion.
A 0/1 DCM m123 point samples a high-width condition at the strong-eluent boundary and complements measured and candidate m123 points at higher PE content.
This second m32 condition is a higher-loading, stronger-PE point paired with 9eec792e8b2ea194dd3c; the pair teaches local condition and loading sensitivity.
The m138 point probes a distinct halogenated hydrophobic structure at 10/1 DCM, adding condition coverage where the model predicts a moderately broad interval.
This m199 point targets a broad predicted region at 1/1 DCM and higher loading, complementing measured late m199 behavior for loading-tail repair.
The broad predicted interval for m203 at 10/1 DCM makes it informative for late-completion calibration in a tertiary alcohol-like chemotype.
This m91 point adds a moderate-width 2/1 DCM condition to a molecule with measured and candidate ratio variation, supporting solvent-response learning.
A 1/1 PE m56 point supplies a local ester control in the PE-rich region and helps distinguish ordinary loading variation from broad-tail behavior.
The 50/1 PE m1 condition extends a hydrophobic bromide response toward weaker elution and tests the model's PE-ratio trend.
High q-widths for m124 at 0/1 DCM target an underconstrained fused aromatic ether region and can repair broad V1/V2 predictions.
This m204 point has very broad predicted targets at 10/1 PE, probing a late polar alcohol region that may generalize to other strongly retained compounds.
The m75 5/1 PE condition provides a moderate-width local label in an ester-rich family and adds coverage distinct from the DCM-heavy records.
This m154 point probes a halogenated aryl ether at 5/1 DCM and adds structural coverage with moderate predicted uncertainty.
The 50/1 PE m14 point is paired with be2d8614d178068a6f1e, forming a wide ratio contrast for learning molecule-specific PE response.
A broad predicted m44 interval at 50/1 DCM targets a late aromatic ketone regime and provides a useful tail label at a weak eluent.
This high-width m103 point at 20/1 DCM samples a polarizable halogenated ester region and tests late-tail behavior at elevated density and loading.
A narrow-width m140 point at 1/1 DCM serves as a stable aromatic iodide control for the broader candidate regions.
The m132 point adds a 50/1 PE condition with moderate widths, extending a simple hydrophobic aromatic response toward weak elution.
This m144 point samples a nitrile-containing aromatic at 10/1 DCM and tests whether the model transfers local response patterns across related aromatic acceptors.
The second m81 point at 1/1 DCM and higher loading forms a local loading/ratio contrast with 36c9891cc52de490659d.
A broad predicted m176 interval at 20/1 DCM targets a chlorinated benzophenone-like structure and adds a late-tail label for a different aromatic ketone environment.
This m2 point at 5/1 DCM supplies a moderate-width dibrominated aromatic control and expands structural coverage without duplicating the highest-width cases.

hypotheses.content: Broad V2 tails and large V2-minus-V1 intervals mark underconstrained structure-condition regions, especially for polar, fused, or strongly adsorbing molecules.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels in these regions can improve completion-volume prediction and reduce systematic underlearning of late tails.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the broad intervals reproducible across related structures and nearby PE/EA ratios, or are they isolated molecule-specific effects?

hypotheses.content: PE/EA ratio, loading amount, and loading-solvent volume interact in molecule-specific ways, so condition response should be learned locally rather than imposed as one global monotonic correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The paired m32, m14, m81, and m163 candidates add repeated-molecule condition contrasts that can teach interaction terms useful across the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched condition changes produce consistent shifts in V1 and V2, or do functional-group environments reverse or amplify the response?

hypotheses.content: Moderate-width local controls are needed alongside high-width cases to distinguish genuine model failure from ordinary interpolation noise and to stabilize retraining across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls such as m149, m52, m140, and m2 provide labels in less extreme regions, helping the retrained model learn a calibrated transition from ordinary to difficult chromatography.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After adding both controls and high-width cases, do predicted widths contract selectively in the difficult regions while preserving accuracy in ordinary regions?

batch_rationale: The batch covers several high-width late-elution regions while retaining moderate-width controls. Repeated molecules m32, m14, and m81 create local condition or loading contrasts; m79, m123, m163, m91, and m56 extend response coverage across solvent ratios. Broad-tail candidates m173, m11, m3, m199, m204, m124, m103, and m176 target underconstrained V2 behavior, while aromatic and halogenated controls improve structural coverage. This combination should help QGeoGNN learn condition interactions and tail behavior while avoiding a batch composed only of extreme predictions.
